lead.tldr: Crypto and AI PAC spending spikes, but voter backlash risk rises as awareness remains low • CLARITY Act advances, promising stablecoin yield certainty, and failure could shift focus to existing compliance frameworks • Bitcoin eyes $79k weekly close, driven by spot ETF inflows and tightening liquidity • Linux root exploit patched, crypto nodes must audit dependencies and consider AI‑enhanced security solutions • Uphold's $5M settlement highlights regulatory scrutiny on crypto lending products, compliance costs likely rise

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Bitcoin surged to a $78k close in April while spot ETF inflows keep momentum alive. Meanwhile, the CLARITY Act pushes for regulatory certainty as New York settles a $5 million Uphold fraud case and a critical Linux bug sparks fresh AI‑driven security efforts.

top_signals.title: Crypto, AI Super PACs Flood Midterms As Poll Finds Most Americans Distrust Both Industries
top_signals.summary: Crypto and AI firms are intensifying political spending, with OpenAI and Anthropic reporting record expenditures in the first quarter of 2026. A Fairshake‑linked political action committee has contributed more than $40 million in an effort to unseat Senator Sherrod Brown, a vocal critic of the crypto industry. The crypto sector is advancing the CLARITY Act in the Senate to obtain clearer regulatory guidance, a move that could affect compliance costs and market stability. A recent poll shows that most Americans distrust both the crypto and AI industries, suggesting a potential backlash that investors should monitor.

top_signals.title: Crypto Industry Will Be ‘Just Fine’ If CLARITY Act Doesn’t Pass: Chris Perkins
top_signals.summary: Chris Perkins said the crypto sector will be “just fine” even if the CLARITY Act does not pass. Industry leaders view the bill as a way to lock in regulatory certainty for stablecoin yields but maintain that the market’s resilience does not hinge on its approval. Several senators are pushing the legislation forward, signaling that policymakers see it as a tool to solidify the regulatory framework for stablecoins.

top_signals.title: Can Bitcoin Seal its Best Weekly Close in Over Three Months?
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin is expected to end the current week near $79,000, which would represent its strongest weekly closing level since January. The price action is being closely monitored by traders who are assessing liquidity conditions and the impact of inflows into spot Bitcoin exchange‑traded funds. Analysts note that the robust ETF inflows could support further upside, but they also warn that a sudden withdrawal of liquidity could reverse the rally.

top_signals.title: Linux Copy Fail: ‘A Trivially Exploitable Bug’
top_signals.summary: A logic bug in Linux that is trivially exploitable was disclosed after a private report and patched in early April. The vulnerability affects major Linux distributions released over the past nine years and can be leveraged by a small Python script to obtain root on any platform, raising concerns for crypto exchanges and blockchain nodes that rely on Linux. The newly launched Project Glasswing aims to harness AI for defensive security against such threats.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Posts Strongest Monthly Gain In 12 months In April
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin posted its biggest monthly rise in a year in April, moving from roughly $66,000 to about $78,190. The price appreciation signals renewed buying pressure that may attract institutional capital seeking exposure to the leading digital asset. However, CryptoQuant cautions that the market could face a multi‑month correction, reflecting ongoing volatility. Some analysts, including Michael van de Poppe, argue that the rally could set the stage for a potential return toward the $100,000 threshold even without a fresh narrative.

top_signals.title: NY Forces Uphold to Pay $5M Over Fraudulent Crypto Product
top_signals.summary: New York Attorney General Letitia James secured a settlement of more than $5 million from the crypto platform Uphold for promoting the fraudulent CredEarn product. CredEarn was advertised as a safe savings vehicle but was actually funded by risky micro‑loans to low‑income gamers in China and provided no insurance coverage. Uphold denies intentional wrongdoing, will compensate victims, and acknowledged that it operated without the broker registration required under New York law, highlighting regulatory compliance risks for crypto service providers.

Perkins argues that the crypto market’s resilience does not depend on a single piece of legislation and that the sector will be “just fine” without it. This optimism is echoed by many founders who see the current regulatory debate as an opportunity to demonstrate maturity and self‑governance.
